price_per_million.source: copied from reasoning_models_v1 (confirmed 2026-11-11); thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: PULL_UP as a counter to defensive coverage
league-wide lift across units (share of units with lift>0, median lift in pp)
defensive suppression and forced play types
regression to the mean and mechanical floor in lift measures
methodological_questions: Can 'PNR fail' be defined from pre-outcome information, or does any available label use the result being measured?
What is the baseline for PULL_UP lift, and is it comparable within unit and context?
Can per-unit lift be estimated reliably enough to support a '>=70% of units positive' criterion?
What is the unit (team-season, player, lineup), and how are confounding, multiplicity and season drift handled?
Do the two thresholds (>=70% positive, median >2pp) have a stated rationale, and what do they imply under sampling noise?

historical_evidence.finding: The A1 adaptation falsification found that the adapter PPP lift (+0.0667) was not clearly better than no_signal (+0.1260) or wrong_way (+0.0111) teams. The adapter-minus-no-signal gap was negative (-0.0361 with 1 vote, -0.1170 with 2 votes), and next-game carryover was not significant (Welch p=0.842). The recorded failure mechanism is a construction, selection or labelling flaw. The limitations listed are label error and selection/regression to the mean. The risks listed are LABEL_ERROR and MECHANICAL_FLOOR.

Within-game 'adapters' gained about +0.048 to +0.058 PPP over non-adapters. The record notes the no-signal baseline had the highest dPPP, and the SWITCH subgroup reversed. The listed limitation is selection or regression to the mean.

A within-scheme re-test controlling for early-PPP selection gave mixed results. The adapter gap was +0.0830 (p=0.0046) for DROP, +0.0539 (p=0.0493) for HELP and -0.0199 (p=0.6514) for SWITCH. Quintile gaps changed sign. DROP carryover was not significant (+0.0039, p=0.4244).

Labelling on-ball coverage (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) from NBA matchup and play-by-play fields reached only 14.9% (DET) and 3.3% (ORL) of on-ball possessions. switches_on was not populated. The verdict was failed_gate.

Descriptive star-suppression work reported Giannis forced into PULL_UP at 0.848 PPP, -0.540 versus his preferred DRIVE. The record notes no placebo or matching, and that later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts. It lists PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE as a risk.

Play-by-play-derived shot-level PNR shares of half-court shots in 2024-25 ranged from about 7.6% (OKC) to 13.8% (IND). The record is descriptive, and possession-level PNR rates are noted to be higher. It is a calibration input, not a test.
Model-implied TOV_FORCE channel lifts shrank by about 50% or more under adversarial re-routing. The record notes the net lift is not observed in games and rests on a small sample (4 games).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Lift in an inferred 'adapter' group, tested against wrong-way and no-signal groups plus carryover
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as an artifact from a construction, selection or labelling flaw, with label error, selection/regression to the mean and mechanical floor as limitations.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Within-game 'did_adapt toward counter' lift measured as later-minus-earlier PPP
failed_approaches.why: Selection or regression to the mean. The no-signal baseline was highest, and the SWITCH subgroup reversed.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labelling defensive coverage from matchup and play-by-play fields
failed_approaches.why: Label rates were 3-15% and switches_on was unpopulated, so the label was not usable at scale.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Reading forced-PULL_UP PPP gaps for stars as evidence of suppression
failed_approaches.why: No placebo or matching. Later work treated similar gaps as artifacts.

evidence_establishes: Earlier work in this project on closely related 'counter lift' questions (A1 adapter lift, within-game adaptation) was recorded as artifact or inconclusive. The apparent lifts came from selection, regression to the mean, label error or mechanical floor.
Coverage labels from matchup and play-by-play fields were recorded as unusable at scale (3-15% label rate, switches_on unpopulated).
The only PULL_UP-specific record is descriptive (a star forced into PULL_UP scored lower than on DRIVE) and had no placebo or matching.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether PULL_UP lifts efficiency after PNR failure league-wide. No retrieved record tests this hypothesis.
Whether a pre-outcome definition of 'PNR fail' exists in these data. No record shows one.
The between-unit variance of true PULL_UP lift, or the split-half reliability of per-unit lift.
Whether the 70% and 2pp thresholds are achievable or meaningful. No record calibrates them.
own_inferences: 'PNR fail' is most likely to be defined from the possession outcome (for example, the ball handler gets a paint touch, a foul, or an open look). That would make the label outcome-derived and would build a mechanical relationship between the 'fail' label and the lift measure.

PULL_UP shots tend to come from the ball handler keeping the ball against a recovering or under-screen defender. Comparing them with other play types, which differ in shot quality and difficulty, mixes shot-selection differences with any counter effect.

With few failed PNR possessions per team-season, per-unit sign tests will be noisy. A 70% positive share can arise from noise alone if the true effect is modest, and can be missed even when the true effect is real. The two criteria are not independent, because a median >2pp makes a large positive share more likely.
Prior records of related lift analyses ending as artifacts raise the prior that a naive version of this test will also produce an artifact.
uncertainties: Which fields could identify defensive coverage or screen outcome before the shot. The data catalog was not consulted, and the possession graph's PNR labels (PBPProxyPNR calibration) are unvalidated here.
The number of PNR-fail possessions per unit, the unit definition, and the shot-level versus possession-level PNR gap.
The 2025-26 playoffs are only partial on the question date (complete from 2026-06-21), so the sample must be frozen.
Whether 'lift' is meant as PPP, eFG or shot-quality difference, and against which counterfactual.

historical_effect.explanation: Without the history I might have proceeded with a simple unit-level lift test. The retrieved records show that similar counter-lift analyses turned out to be artifacts (selection, regression to the mean, label error, mechanical floor) and that coverage labels were unusable at scale. I therefore require a pre-outcome failure definition, within-unit difference-in-differences against non-fail PNR possessions, split-sample reliability and a placebo. I also lowered the probability of a clean 'supported' result.

blocking_constraints.text: Any 'PNR fail' definition based on the possession result, shot quality or paint touch makes the label depend on the outcome of the PULL_UP lift.
Coverage and screen-outcome labels were recorded as unusable at scale (3-15% coverage in FAM:SF-APPS-058), and PNR labels come from a proxy classifier.
Per-unit lift may be too noisy to support a '>=70% of units positive' criterion unless the true effect is large and units have many failed-PNR possessions.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests PULL_UP as a counter to PNR failure. Related adaptation and counter-lift work was recorded as artifact or inconclusive, coverage labelling was recorded as untestable, and the PULL_UP evidence is descriptive and unmatched.

risks.text: Defining PNR failure from the result of the possession, and then measuring PULL_UP lift on the same possessions, builds in the effect.
PULL_UP shots after a beaten defender, or under a drop scheme, have a different baseline than other play types, so lift can reflect where the defence allowed the shot rather than a counter effect.
Units chosen or conditioned on weak earlier PPP, or possessions conditioned on a failure label, will show regression to the mean, as recorded in FAM:SF13 and FAM:SF-APPA-001.
Small per-unit counts of failed-PNR PULL_UP possessions make the sign of per-unit lift mostly noise. The 70% criterion is sensitive to that noise.
The PNR proxy classifier and play-type labels are unvalidated, and coverage labels reached only 3-15% in prior work.
Player quality, defender, score and clock state, lineup, scheme and shot location affect both the choice to pull up and its efficiency.
PULL_UP frequency and efficiency differ by player type and context, so comparing raw rates across units mixes composition effects.
Choices of unit, season, definition of failure and lift measure give many possible analyses unless one primary specification is fixed before the data are examined.
Four seasons and playoffs are pooled, and scheme usage and shot selection drift across seasons and between regular season and playoffs.
Descriptive PULL_UP gaps (FAM:SF-CHT-009) had no placebo, and a null comparison is needed before any gap can be read as a counter effect.

design.estimand: For each offensive unit u, the difference-in-differences of efficiency (points per possession, with eFG as a secondary measure) between PULL_UP and the best-pre-registered alternative finish (for example DRIVE) on PNR possessions flagged failed by a pre-outcome rule, minus the same PULL_UP-minus-alternative difference on non-failed PNR possessions. Lift is expressed in pp (PPP*100 or eFG points). The claim is supported only if the shrunken (empirical Bayes) per-unit lift is >0 in >=70% of units and the median lift is >2pp.
design.unit: Primary: offensive team-season with >=N_min qualifying failed-PNR possessions (N_min to be set from the reliability analysis below). Secondary: ball-handler-season. Unit definitions are fixed before any outcome is examined.
design.sample: Regular seasons 2022-23 to 2024-25 plus the complete 2025-26 regular season (complete 2026-04-13), as the confirmation window. Playoffs are analysed separately. The 2025-26 playoffs are partial on 2026-05-23 and excluded until complete (2026-06-21). Define 'PNR fail' using only information available before the shot (for example, the ball handler's separation or position at the screen if it can be derived, or the screen-defender pairing from matchup fields) and not shot result, shot quality or points. If no pre-outcome definition can be built from the available fields, stop and record 'untestable' with the label rate reported, as in FAM:SF-APPS-058.
design.power: Before looking at outcomes, compute the distribution of failed-PNR possessions per unit and the split-half (odd/even game) reliability of per-unit lift. Estimate the between-unit SD of true lift by random-effects meta-analysis. Simulate the probability that a true median of 2pp yields >=70% positive observed signs at the observed per-unit sample sizes. If that probability is below 0.8, or split-half reliability is below 0.5, the criterion is not testable and a pooled or hierarchical estimate with a credible interval replaces the sign-share criterion.
design.controls: Condition on defender and offensive-player identity (or quality), lineup, score margin, clock and period, shot zone and distance, season, and home/away. Use within-unit non-failed PNR possessions as the baseline to net out mechanical floor. Report shrunken estimates to handle regression to the mean, and use a held-out season (2025-26) to avoid selecting thresholds on the discovery data.
design.falsification: (1) Placebo: assign the 'fail' label to random PNR possessions within game and context (permutation), and expect no lift. (2) Negative-control play type: run the same test for a type with no hypothesised counter role (for example SPOT_UP). (3) Label robustness: re-run with two alternative pre-outcome fail definitions and with a stricter, higher-precision subset. (4) Carryover: lift in earlier games should predict later games for the same unit (compare with FAM:SF-APPA-001, where carryover p=0.842). (5) Sign-flip check: no result if lift disappears once non-fail baselines are used.
design.multiplicity: One primary specification (unit, fail definition, lift measure and alternative finish fixed in advance). All secondary and sensitivity analyses are labelled exploratory, with Holm correction across the pre-registered secondary set and false-discovery-rate control for any unit-level claims.
design.decision_rule: Supported if, in the held-out confirmation window, the shrunken lift is >0 in >=70% of units, the median lift exceeds 2pp with a 95% interval excluding 0, the placebo and negative-control results are null, and discovery and confirmation agree in sign. Rejected if the pooled lift's 95% interval excludes 2pp on the low side and power is adequate. Untestable if the fail label cannot be built without the outcome, or reliability is too low. Artifact if the effect vanishes under the placebo, non-fail baseline or alternative definitions. Otherwise uncertain.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game play-by-play, rotation, matchup and box-score files, plus the possession graph built from them. Seasons 2022-23 to 2024-25 complete; 2025-26 regular season complete (from 2026-04-13); 2025-26 playoffs excluded until complete (2026-06-21). Freeze the extraction date, classifier version (PBPProxyPNR) and play-type labels before analysis.

research_concepts: pull-up jump shot as counter to defensive coverage
unit-level lift in points per possession (percentage points)
methodological_questions: How should PNR 'fail' be defined without using the outcome or leaking look-ahead information?
Is lift of PULL_UP versus alternative actions measured against a valid baseline within comparable units (team, player, lineup)?
Is a 70% share of units with positive lift and median lift above 2pp achievable given sample sizes, regression to the mean and the mechanical floor?
How are the units defined and how are confounding, multiple testing and drift across seasons handled?
args.query: Pre-registered test of whether PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter when pick-and-roll defense fails: share of units with lift>0 (>=70%) and median lift>2pp, with attention to outcome-derived labels, selection and reliability

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}
